How much does it cost to run a streaming box?

A typical streaming box uses about 15 watts (5–40W depending on the model). Used for 4 hours per use, 7 uses a week, it costs about 1.6p per use and £5.75 a year at the current price cap rate.

Cost per use
1.6p
About £5.75 a year at 4 hours per use, 7 uses a week.

Standing charge not included.

Adjust for yours
Ofgem price cap average for 1 Oct – 31 Dec 2026 (standard variable tariff, Direct Debit, England, Scotland & Wales).

About these figures

Worth knowing: CSE lists TV box 40W.

Source for the typical figure: CSE 'What uses watt?' table. See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Switch off at the wall rather than leaving devices on standby.
  • Turn down screen brightness; it's often the biggest single draw on a TV.
  • Use power-saving or eco modes on consoles and computers.

Questions

How much does it cost to run a streaming box per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 15W model costs about 0.4p an hour while it's running.

How much does it cost to run a streaming box per year?

About £5.75 a year, based on 4 hours per use, 7 uses a week. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my streaming box's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
